Article Title: Midterm blues: Why a 'lame' duck Donald Trump may push for a quick India-US trade deal
Article Text:
Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. (Image for representative purpose only)

What this means for India-US trade deal

What does Democrats’ win in US midterm elections mean for India-US trade deal prospects? Will Donald Trump be forced to change his strategy?The unfavourable midterm election outcome is unlikely to prompt President Donald Trump to change course on trade, according to an analysis by Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).But, it’s important to note that both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and the strengthening of supply chains.Democratic lawmakers, too, favour protective tariffs to safeguard unionised workers and local industries.“The adverse midterm results won’t change President Donald Trump’s trade direction because both Democrats and Republicans now favor economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing, and strong supply chains,” says Ajay Srivastava, founder of GTRI.Unable to rely on Congress for every measure, Trump is expected to continue exercising powers already available to the administration. These include Sections 232 and 301, along with executive orders, Treasury sanctions and rules issued by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), to exert unilateral pressure on trading partners.According to GTRI, with foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win.“Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout,” he says.For several months, leaders on both sides have indicated that a trade agreement is close to being finalised. However, the lack of clarity over the US offer appears to have held up its completion, the think tank says.Trump is now likely to use his executive authority to push India towards an early agreement that opens up the Indian market to American agricultural and industrial products, while securing other significant concessions for US businesses.The agreement under negotiation between India and the US is fundamentally different from the other free trade agreements (FTAs) India has entered into. Under conventional trade agreements, both participating countries reduce or eliminate their regular import duties, which are governed by World Trade Organization (WTO) rules and referred to as Most Favoured Nation (MFN) tariffs.The proposed US–India framework, however, follows a different approach. Washington would continue to levy its regular MFN duties, while India would be required to eliminate or lower such tariffs on most industrial products and a wide range of agricultural goods.The February 6 US–India Joint Statement sets out further commitments for India. These include aligning its security and economic policies with Washington, purchasing $500 billion worth of American goods over five years, and relaxing domestic regulatory oversight of imports from the US.“The US may be relying on the threat of additional tariffs to secure India's compliance. These include potential measures linked to India's purchases of Russian oil under the Graham Act and Section 301,” Srivastava notes.Also, signing the agreement would not necessarily protect India from further tariff action. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion.“India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement. Opening its markets, committing to large purchases and limiting its policy choices would carry lasting costs, while any U.S. tariff relief could prove temporary. New Delhi should insist on clear, enforceable reciprocal concessions, consistency with WTO rules and full freedom to protect its energy security and development priorities. The pressure to announce a deal must not outweigh the need to secure one that serves India’s long-term interests,” Srivastava says.
Article Summary: Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion. India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement.

Article Title: Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows as Trump loses US midterm elections
Article Text:
Crude prices fall below $100 per barrel

Trump faces pressure as war weighs on Republicans

Qatar steps up mediation as Iran deal remains distant

Oil prices continued to ease on Thursday, with Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) tumbling below the $100-per-barrel threshold.Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90, as markets continued to react to the political fallout of the US midterm elections and the possibility of an end to the war with Iran.Brent crude futures fell 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 a barrel, while WTI crude declined 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.The latest movement follows Wednesday's sharp sell-off, when both benchmarks lost more than 8% and settled at their lowest levels in over two months. Brent ended the session at $94.62 a barrel, shedding $8.98 or 8.7%, while WTI settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3%. Both contracts recorded their lowest closing levels since August 31.The market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that US President Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.The election outcome has also complicated Washington's options in the conflict. With Democrats taking control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump could find it harder to pursue further military action.Two sources close to Gulf government circles told Reuters that the weakened political position gave him greater reason to pursue a negotiated settlement, making a full-scale assault on Iran less likely.However, the possibility of a deal does not necessarily rule out further escalation. Gulf analysts said an agreement that allows Iran to claim a clear victory while leaving Trump appearing defeated could encourage recklessness rather than restraint.Trump told the Financial Times earlier this week that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran. A day later, he acknowledged that the conflict had contributed to his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections.Vice president JD Vance also questioned the decision to enter the war on Wednesday, distancing himself from it and blaming the conflict entirely for the Republicans' electoral setback.Tehran, however, has indicated that a change in political control in Washington would not alter its position towards the US. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that American hostility would continue regardless of which party was in power.There were also fresh developments in the region, with Yemen's Houthis claiming to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.Diplomatic efforts to prevent another escalation have gathered pace, with Qatar stepping up mediation following the US elections. But the prospect of an immediate breakthrough remains uncertain.Meanwhile, regional energy flows continue to be disrupted. The United Arab Emirates is also looking at ways to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, considering a third oil pipeline.Separately, US oil stockpiles recorded a decline last week. The Energy Information Administration said crude inventories dropped by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels in the week ended October 30. This was sharply different from expectations in a Reuters poll, where analysts had forecast an increase of 877,000 barrels.
Article Summary: Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90. Market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.

Article Title: Trump tariff taxes Republicans: What US midterm results mean for Indian H-1B visa holders, Russian oil & trade deal
Article Text:
American voters have handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party.

The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US - so what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look:

What it means for H-1B visa holders and green card aspirants

India’s purchase of Russian oil

India-US trade deal & tariffs

US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections with Republicans losing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.In a significant rebuke to Trump, American voters on Tuesday handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party and shifted several key gubernatorial positions in closely watched elections.Trump's Republican Party suffered major defeats in its strongholds, including Texas, Georgia and Iowa, losing the governors' offices to Democratic candidates.Trump’s policies are being blamed by many as the reason for the loss - with tariffs and inflation in focus.US President Donald Trump has tightened access to H-1B visas through a $100,000 fee and a wage-weighted selection system, making it harder for Indian professionals to secure US jobs. His administration has also suspended eight technology companies from the PERM green card programme, disrupting some workers’ routes to permanent residency and green cards. So will the midterm results change that attitude?No. Not much is expected to change on this front, despite Trump’s loss. This is because both Democrats and Republicans prioritise domestic employment.According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), tighter immigration policies find bipartisan support.“Be it the Biden administration or the Trump one, policies are increasingly becoming restrictive and that approach is unlikely to change,” Srivastava tells TOI.Also Read | ‘Death by restriction’: As Trump sours H-1B visa dream, which Indian IT professionals face the biggest hit? According to Rajiv Dabhadkar, Founder, National Organization For Software and Technology Professionals, the H-1B debate has moved beyond party politics to a fundamental US policy challenge: protecting American jobs while retaining access to global talent.“Regardless of the outcome of the midterm elections, the US is looking to address long-standing flaws in the immigration system, including wage protections, worker displacement and how employers use foreign professionals,” he tells TOI.What fundamentally needs to be understood is that H-1B reform is now a bipartisan American policy imperative, not merely a political reaction to one administration, he adds.Earlier this year, the Donald Trump administration managed to get support for the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The Act allows the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries importing oil from Russia and Iran in a big way.India and China lead the lot of Russian oil buyers. Recently, Trump announced a waiver on those tariffs for India. But, it’s important to note that the waiver was only for a period of 60 days.Also Read | Does Trump’s 60-day tariff waiver really give relief to India? What it means for US trade deal & oil prices The Republicans losing control of the Congress is unlikely to change the Trump administration’s stance on buyers of Russian crude oil. This is because the bill enjoyed bipartisan support - both Democrats and Republicans appear keen to penalise buyers of Russian oil.However, what may work in India’s favour for now is America’s own diesel deal with Russia and the need by the Trump administration and even the Democrats to keep oil prices in check. Sanctioning Russian oil or penalising buyers of Moscow’s crude will not help that cause.So, for now India continues to enjoy relief from the prospect of 100% tariffs for its crude oil procurement from Russia, but this may work as a pressure tactic by the US to finalise a trade deal.For India, which is still negotiating a trade agreement with the United States, the outcome of the midterm elections could strengthen the case for taking a cautious, wait-and-watch approach.Earlier this month, Commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the India-US trade agreement was in the final stages of drafting. However, he stressed that New Delhi would move ahead only if the terms gave Indian exporters an edge over their competitors.India and the US have already finalised a framework for the first phase of the Bilateral Trade Agreement. However, changes in the US tariff environment have led to further negotiations. India is seeking tariff rates on its exports that are more favourable than those faced by competing countries.In the meantime, experts believe the midterm setback could prompt Trump to pursue an early trade agreement with India. They said that with Washington struggling to exercise foreign policy leverage over Russia, China and Iran, Trump may look for quick success on the trade front.However, the economic think tank GTRI said the unfavourable midterm outcome was unlikely to fundamentally alter Trump's trade policy. Both Republicans and Democrats, it noted, support economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and robust supply chains."With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win. Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout and the midterm losses may push Trump to seek a quick India trade deal," said Ajay Srivastava.Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) president SC Ralhan said the US continues to be an important destination for Indian goods and services."What will matter to Indian exporters in the months ahead is how US policy on tariffs and market access takes shape. MSMEs in particular need predictable trading conditions to price orders confidently and plan shipments months in advance," he told PTI.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections. Republicans lost control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US. So what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look.

Article Title: Insurance agent deposited Rs 35 lakh in cash collected as policy premiums; tax officer called it unexplained money saying his name was missing from some policies, why ITAT Jaipur gave full relief
Article Text:
The tax officer noticed discrepancies while examining the insurance documents that the man submitted to support his explanation. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT Jaipur rule in favour of insurance agent?

An insurance agent based in Rajasthan came under the Income Tax Department ’s scrutiny for alleged unexplained cash deposits in his bank account. The agent claimed these were payments for premiums of policyholders.The tax department however believed he had insufficient evidence to prove his claims and sent him a notice. Here is how he ultimately won relief in ITAT Jaipur:The insurance agent in the case deposited Rs 35 lakh in cash into his bank account. The department classified the amount as “unexplained money” and sought details of its source.The man maintained that the cash was not his personal money but represented insurance premiums collected from customers who had bought policies through him.However, the tax officer noticed discrepancies while examining the insurance documents that the man submitted to support his explanation.In some instances, the policies named other individuals as the insurance agents. Asked to explain why the paperwork did not consistently identify him as the agent, the man said he had entered into commission-sharing arrangements with agents associated with other insurance companies.He explained that restrictions under the Insurance Act, which permit an agent to represent only one insurance company at a time, had led him to work with agents from other companies to meet his customers’ requirements. This arrangement, he said, helped him continue serving his existing clients and retain his established customer base.According to an ET report, he further submitted that he received commissions through these agents and that the transactions were routed through banking channels. To substantiate his account, the man produced affidavits from the agents concerned, who confirmed the facts stated by him on oath.The explanation, however, failed to convince the income tax officer in Alwar, who initiated proceedings against the insurance agent over alleged tax evasion and the possession of unexplained cash.Challenging the department’s action, the man first approached the Commissioner of Appeals before taking the matter to the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Jaipur.On October 1, 2026, the ITAT Jaipur ruled in the insurance agent’s favour.Chartered Accountant Ashish Niraj, Partner at ASN & Company, told ET that the man succeeded because he produced detailed evidence that the lower authorities had not effectively rebutted.The documents established that the cash deposits of Rs 35,08,550 were from insurance premiums collected as part of his regular business activities.According to Niraj, the man submitted policy registers, cash flow statements and bank records to demonstrate how the money had moved through the business and ultimately reached the insurance companies.The appearance of other agents’ names on certain policies was another issue raised by the tax authorities. The insurance agent however clarified that, because the Insurance Act restricts an agent to one general insurance company, he had relied on commission-sharing arrangements with agents representing other insurers to continue serving his customers.He supported this explanation with sworn affidavits from the agents involved, along with bank statements showing that commission payments had been made to them through cheques.The man also demonstrated that the receipts recorded during the corresponding period in the preceding year were in a similar range to those during the demonetisation period. This evidence helped persuade the ITAT to accept his explanation and rule in his favour.In practical terms, policyholders should avoid paying insurance premiums in cash. Under the applicable provision, no person can receive Rs 2 lakh or more in cash from another person in a single day, through one transaction, or in connection with a single event or occasion. The penalty is equivalent to the amount received and is imposed on the recipient, which could be the insurer, broker or agent, rather than the person making the payment.This restriction on cash receipts took effect on April 1, 2017, and therefore did not apply to the year involved in this case. The provision is applicable to transactions taking place today.In its remand report, the income tax officer pointed out that several insurance documents named individuals other than the man as the agents. The officer also observed that the man had not produced evidence to support his claim that he had received cash from different individuals for insurance-related purposes during the demonetisation period. This was considered significant because transactions involving the demonetised Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes, classified as illegal tender, had been prohibited at the time.The insurance agent’s lawyer argued that accepting demonetised currency and failing to comply with the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) notification did not automatically amount to a violation of income tax law. According to the lawyer, the man had merely acted as an intermediary and had not accepted the demonetised notes for his personal benefit.After considering the submissions, the ITAT Jaipur found that the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A), had not adequately examined the man’s explanations on two key points: why his name did not appear as the agent on certain insurance policies, and how he had accounted for the cash deposited during the demonetisation period.The Tribunal held that there was no merit in the CIT(A)'s decision to treat the man’s explanation regarding the source of the cash deposited in his bank account as unsatisfactory.According to the ITAT Jaipur, the CIT(A) had rejected the man’s explanation primarily because his name did not appear in the insurance policies as the agent. The Tribunal criticised this approach, observing: “This finding of the CIT(A) is clearly not based on appreciation of the explanation furnished of the same by the assessee (Sharma), noted by us duly substantiated with evidence.”On the question of demonetised currency, the Tribunal held that the man’s inability to produce evidence specifically establishing that he had collected the premiums in the form of the discontinued notes was not, by itself, sufficient reason to reject his explanation for the bank deposits.The ITAT Jaipur accordingly set aside the CIT(A)'s order and directed that the addition of Rs 35,08,550 made to the man’s income be deleted.
Article Summary: Insurance agent in Rajasthan came under the Income Tax Department’s scrutiny for alleged unexplained cash deposits in his bank account. The tax department however believed he had insufficient evidence to prove his claims and sent him a notice. On October 1, 2026, the ITAT Jaipur ruled in the insurance agent’S favour.

Article Title: Tata Sons chair Chandrasekaran meets Italy PM Meloni after Iveco takeover
Article Text:
Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran meets Italian PM Meloni after Iveco acquisition

NEW DELHI: Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran met Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni at Palazzo Chigi in Rome, with the Indian conglomerate's acquisition of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group featuring prominently in their discussions.The meeting comes as India and Italy look to deepen their strategic industrial and economic ties. Sources said that Chandrasekaran presented the Tata Group's strategy following its acquisition of a controlling stake in Iveco, one of Italy's leading commercial vehicle manufacturers.On October 30, Tata Motors announced that it had acquired an 89.42 per cent stake in Iveco for nearly 3.43 billion euros following the initial settlement of its cash tender offer. The Italian manufacturer has now become an indirect subsidiary of Tata Motors.The acquisition brings together two companies looking to expand their volumes, revenues and margins significantly over the next five years. Addressing a global press conference at Iveco's headquarters in Turin on Tuesday, Chandrasekaran said the partnership would help create a global commercial vehicle powerhouse.He also acknowledged the support extended by the Italian government during the acquisition process, thanking Meloni and Minister Adolfo Urso for their encouragement."Iveco Group, with very strong Italian roots and a strong presence across Europe and Latin America, brings huge industrial heritage, iconic brands, technology and world-class capabilities across trucks, buses and power trains. I would like to thank everyone who has been involved in this transaction, and I'm grateful to all of them. I would also like to start today by thanking the Italian government and the Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Minister Adolfo Urso for their encouragement and support throughout this process," the Tata Sons chairman said.Chandrasekaran also spoke about Tata Motors' long association with Turin, tracing it back to the development of the company's first indigenous passenger car. He recalled how former chairman Ratan Tata had chosen the Italian city for the project, with the car's design taking shape at the Turin-based design house Idea in the late 1990s."I would like to give you a story which explains our connect with Turin. When our ex-Chairman Mr Ratan Tata decided that Tata Motors will develop and manufacture its indigenous passenger car, he actually turned to Turin, and there was a famous design house in Turin by the name Idea. And Idea was where the first indigenous Indian car took shape. It is from the late nineties that many of us from Tata Motors have been coming to Turin. Therefore, we have a very strong connect with Turin. We owe it to Turin for our passenger car business because it was kind of born here," Chandrasekaran added.The two companies said their complementary product portfolios and geographical strengths would give the combined business a presence in more than 130 countries, covering key developed and high-growth markets across Europe, India, South America, Asia, the Middle East and Africa.Their combined revenues stand at 21 billion euros, or about Rs 2,28,000 crore, according to a joint statement.The acquisition process is still continuing, with Tata Motors and Iveco now moving into the next phase of integration and joint strategic planning.
Article Summary: Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran meets Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Meeting comes as India and Italy look to deepen their strategic industrial and economic ties. Tata Motors acquired an 89.42 per cent stake in Iveco for nearly 3.43 billion euros.

Article Title: Smartphones could get 30% costlier! How AI is driving up prices of your next upgrade
Article Text:
Smartphones to get costlier

AI's appetite for memory is driving up costs

Budget smartphones could take the biggest hit

Affordable phones lose market share

Older chips could replace the latest processors

NEW DELHI: Thinking of buying a new smartphone? You might want to hurry!Artificial intelligence has already shaken up your work life, changed your daily task flows and even sparked conversations about jobs and the future of work. Now, it is about to hit your budgets.The AI boom could soon make buying a new smartphone more expensive, particularly if you are eyeing a budget device. Rising memory costs, fuelled by the artificial intelligence industry's growing appetite for components, could push prices of low-end smartphones up by around 30 per cent, forcing buyers to either postpone their upgrades or consider second-hand phones, according to a report by Jefferies.The growing demand for memory components from AI companies is putting pressure on global supplies, with the technology expected to account for around 60 per cent of memory demand in CY27. The spending plans of AI players could make matters worse. These companies are targeting capital expenditure of around $1.5 trillion in the same year, which could keep memory prices elevated for several more quarters.The impact is already showing up in the cost of smartphone components.According to Jefferies, memory prices are expected to peak by mid-CY27, but manufacturers are already dealing with a sharp increase in costs."Memory cost per unit is likely to have surged ~3x, from est $20 in CY25 to est $60-65 now," the report said.If you thought rising memory costs would affect all smartphones equally, the affordable segment has a bigger problem. For Android smartphones priced below $200, memory accounts for around 60 per cent of the total bill of materials, making these devices particularly vulnerable to price increases.Manufacturers may have little choice but to pass on some of the higher costs to buyers. The report warned that "a price hike of ~30% in low-end phones could defer new purchases or trigger second-hand affordable purchases".That could mean consumers putting off their next smartphone upgrade or looking at pre-owned devices instead. Manufacturers, too, may have to rethink their affordable offerings by reducing the number of lower-priced variants and downsizing their distribution channels to manage rising input costs.The rising cost of components could also weigh on the overall smartphone market. Jefferies expects global smartphone shipments to decline by 15 per cent annually to 1,067 million units in CY26 and 911 million units in CY27.While the report has slightly raised its shipment forecasts for CY26 and CY27 by 5 per cent and 3 per cent, respectively, the broader outlook remains weak.The affordable segment is expected to bear the biggest brunt. Its share of the global smartphone market could fall from 42 per cent in CY25 to 24 per cent in CY26. Meanwhile, the share of smartphones priced above $600 could rise from 29 per cent to 38 per cent over the same period.Memory is not the only component creating headaches for smartphone manufacturers. The report identified semiconductor shortages as the biggest supply-chain bottleneck, adding to the pressure on the industry.To contain costs, manufacturers are considering using chips that are one to two years old instead of the latest flagship processors.The challenges could also have a longer-term impact on the industry. Even if smartphone demand recovers rapidly from CY28, manufacturers may struggle to restore shipment levels if they reduce production capacity during the current slowdown, the report cautioned.
Article Summary: Rising memory costs, fuelled by the artificial intelligence industry's growing appetite for components, could push prices of low-end smartphones up by around 30 per cent. The impact is already showing up in the cost of smartphone components. Manufacturers may have to pass on some of the higher costs to buyers.

Article Title: Dubai Duty Free to offer discounts on UPI payments
Article Text:
NPCI International Payments has unveiled a delightful discount for Indian travelers shopping at Dubai Duty Free.

MUMBAI: NPCI International Payments (NIPL), the international arm of NPCI, has announced a 10% discount of up to AED 100 for Indian travellers shopping at Dubai Duty Free outlets when they pay through UPI. The offer covers eligible purchases at participating outlets at Dubai International Airport and Al Maktoum International Airport.Travellers must activate UPI International or UPI Global through their UPI-enabled app and link an eligible Indian bank account to make payments. Network International will act as the acquiring partner, enabling UPI acceptance at participating payment terminals and processing transactions. Dubai Duty Free sells products across categories such as fashion, beauty, electronics, confectionery, beverages, watches and jewellery.The initiative is aimed at expanding UPI acceptance across retail outlets in the UAE and strengthening digital payment connectivity between India and the UAE.According to Ritesh Shukla, MD & CEO of NPCI International, the initiative aims to encourage wider UPI adoption by offering Indian travellers a familiar payment option overseas."Through this initiative, we aim to encourage wider adoption of UPI while elevating the overall journey for Indian visitors," he said.According to Murat Cagri Suzer, group CEO of Network International, the partnership will connect international payment schemes with local acceptance points in the UAE. "We are giving Indian visitors a familiar, secure way to pay as they shop. This reflects the flexibility and innovation at the core of our acquiring infrastructure – connecting international payment schemes to local acceptance points, reliably and at scale," he said.According to Ramesh Cidambi, managing director of Dubai Duty Free, the integration will allow Indian travellers to use a familiar payment method while shopping at the airports. "The integration of UPI provides Indian travellers with a familiar, secure and seamless way to pay while enjoying the benefits of this exclusive offer," he said.
Article Summary: NPCI International Payments has announced a 10% discount for Indian travellers shopping at Dubai Duty Free outlets when they pay through UPI. The offer covers eligible purchases at Dubai International Airport and Al Maktoum International Airport. The initiative is aimed at expanding UPI acceptance across retail outlets in the UAE.

Article Title: Media house Sanmarg acquires Tehelka.com, plans to relaunch magazine as weekly
Article Text:
As part of its revival plans, Sanmarg intends to convert Tehelka from a fortnightly to a weekly publication while continuing to publish in both print and digital formats.

City-based media group Sanmarg Private Limited has acquired a 100 per cent stake in Tehelka.com Private Limited, marking its entry into the magazine segment and strengthening its presence in the digital media landscape.The group, which publishes a prominent Hindi daily, said it plans to invest further in the publication, known for its investigative journalism, and restore its past reputation while maintaining high standards of journalistic integrity and credibility.As part of its revival plans, Sanmarg intends to convert Tehelka from a fortnightly to a weekly publication while continuing to publish in both print and digital formats.Tehelka had been known for its pioneering role in sting journalism in India in the early 2000s.The acquisition was completed last month from a group of investors who had owned Tehelka.com since 2017, Sanmarg said in a statement on Wednesday.Arvind Chaturvedi has been appointed chief editor to lead the publication's new journey.The acquisition includes all assets of Tehelka.com Private Limited, including its print and digital operations and intellectual property dating back to 2017, the statement said.Sanmarg said it would honour commitments to the publication's 276 lifetime subscribers, who were also its founding members, and continue providing them with print copies and digital subscription access, as applicable.The group said it would also ensure compliance with all applicable government rules and regulations.The state outlined the ownership history of Tehelka, stating that its previous owner, Anant Media Pvt Ltd, had transferred its intellectual property, title, employees and operational assets to Tehelka.com Private Limited around 2016.Anant Media had retained responsibility for previous litigations and related liabilities, the statement said, adding that Tehelka.com subsequently lost access to its archives, past footage, old copies and several other intellectual properties.In 2017, a group of investors acquired the entire shareholding of Tehelka.com Private Limited and facilitated the exit of the magazine's former editor Tarun Tejpal and other minority investors, it said.The investors also confirmed that Tejpal had no involvement in Tehelka or its operations, according to the statement.Sanmarg said its acquisition was aimed at preserving Tehelka's legacy while adapting the publication to the changing needs of modern journalism and digital audiences.
Article Summary: City-based media group Sanmarg Private Limited has acquired a 100 per cent stake in Tehelka.com Private Limited. The group, which publishes a prominent Hindi daily, said it plans to invest further in the publication, known for its investigative journalism. As part of its revival plans, Sanmarg intends to convert TehelKA from a fortnightly to a weekly publication.

Article Title: Noel Tata moves to induct Choksey onto NCPA board
Article Text:
The trust is the largest shareholder in Tata Sons, with a 28% stake

MUMBAI: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has moved to bring Vera Choksey (née Tata), a shareholder in Tata Sons and sister of HDFC Bank executive director Jimmy Tata, onto the board of Mumbai’s National Centre for the Performing Arts (NCPA), according to people familiar with the matter.Noel wrote to NCPA chairman Khushroo N Suntook on Wednesday proposing Choksey’s appointment as a nominee of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, the people said.The trust is the largest shareholder in Tata Sons, with a 28% stake, and has long backed institutions such as the NCPA. Choksey, daughter of the late Minocher Tata and Piloo Tata, is a member of the Tata family descended from founder Jamsetji Tata.She, her brother Jimmy, their mother Piloo and the MK Tata Trust, established by their late father Minocher, together own about 1% of Tata Sons.The MK Tata Trust, of which Vera is a trustee, is dependent on dividends from Tata Sons to fund its charitable activities, much like SDTT. However, with Tata Sons unable to complete its annual general meeting because of legal and regulatory roadblocks, shareholders have been unable to vote on and approve the proposed dividend, delaying payouts to shareholder trusts.Apart from Suntook, the NCPA board, which has more than a dozen members, includes Noel, former Citi India CEO Pramit Jhaveri, Tata Trusts’ trustee Jehangir Jehangir, Brinda Khatau, Nirmal Bhogilal of the Batliboi family, Sir Dinshaw Maneckjee Petit, Jehangir Sorabjee, son of the late jurist Soli Sorabjee, and industrialist Jamshyd Godrej.
Article Summary: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has moved to bring Vera Choksey (née Tata) onto the board of Mumbai’s National Centre for the Performing Arts. The trust is the largest shareholder in Tata Sons, with a 28% stake, and has long backed institutions such as the NCPA.

Article Title: Democratic win may soften US immigration rhetoric; no immediate H-1B relief
Article Text:
Visa

Bengaluru: A Democratic majority in Congress may shift the tone of the US immigration debate, but it is unlikely to bring immediate policy relief for Indian technology professionals or employers.However, experts believe a Democratic victory could help temper anti-immigrant sentiment and the political rhetoric targeting Indian technology professionals, creating a more favourable environment for skilled immigration and potentially laying the groundwork for policy changes in the longer term.Stephen Yale-Loehr, retired professor of immigration law practice at Cornell Law School, said a change in congressional control would not immediately translate into immigration reform.“President Trump is still president, and he controls the immigration agencies. Even if the Democrats pass positive immigration laws, President Trump can veto them. However, the Democrats can hold hearings and investigations to try to persuade the US public that immigration benefits, not hurts, the country. That way they will lay the groundwork for possible true immigration reform in 2029, assuming the Democrats control Congress then and there is a Democratic president then,” he said.David J Bier, director of Immigration Studies at Cato Institute, echoed this assessment, saying the election outcome would have almost no immediate impact on immigration policy. “It will have almost no immediate effect because Republicans still have enough votes to block most immigration bills in the Senate, and even if they didn’t, Trump would veto bills that block his agenda,” he said. Cyrus D Mehta, managing partner of New York-based law firm Cyrus D Mehta & Partners, said that even if Democrats take control of both houses of Congress, Trump would retain executive powers and could issue rules supporting the increase in H-1B fees to more than $100,000, along with other restrictions on the H-1B and green card programmes.“Trump will not be able to get legislation through Congress to endorse his executive actions if there are no Republican majorities. In any event, it would have been difficult for him to do so even now without 60 votes in the Senate. If the new Democratic majorities pass bills in Congress in 2026, Trump will have the power to veto them,” Mehta said.However, he said, officials in the Trump administration would face greater scrutiny and would need to justify their positions and policies before congressional oversight committees. If the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) denies H-1B petitions without justifiable grounds, such decisions could also come under investigation.“Also, since Texas and Georgia have become Democratic, they will no longer side with Trump in litigation against the $100,000 fee. This will leave the administration with less support in defending its policies in court,” he said.For Indian IT companies, which have traditionally relied on H-1B visas to deploy skilled professionals to the US, the debate comes amid a gradual shift towards local hiring and a reduced dependence on overseas work visas. Indian technology companies have significantly expanded their US-based workforce over the years, building a stronger domestic talent pool.According to IT industry body Nasscom, the number of H-1B visas issued to leading Indian and India-centric companies fell from 14,792 in 2015 to 10,162 in 2024. India’s largest IT services company, TCS, had around 11,000 H-1B employees within its 32,000-33,000-strong US workforce as of October last year.Microsoft said 80% of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications it filed in the last fiscal year were for extensions or changes in the status of existing employees. Applications for new hires accounted for just 1% of its US workforce and involved individuals already legally present in the country.Nasscom has maintained that H-1B is a high-skilled worker mobility programme and a non-immigrant visa that helps bridge critical skills gaps in the US. Indian technology companies contribute about $103 billion to the US economy and support more than 500,000 jobs across over 25 states, according to the industry body.Research has also challenged the argument that H-1B visa holders displace American workers. National Foundation for American Policy’s (NFAP) latest research cited a study by economist Madeline Zavodny, which found that H-1B visa holders do not adversely affect US workers. Instead, their presence is associated with lower unemployment rates and faster earnings growth among college graduates, including recent graduates.The research also found that a one-percentage-point increase in the share of workers with H-1B visas in an occupation was associated with an increase of 0.1 to 0.26 percentage points in the earnings growth rate for workers in that occupation.Other research cited by NFAP suggests that restricting H-1B visas could also have wider employment consequences. It estimated that if 178,000 H-1B applications had not been rejected in 2007 and 2008 because of the annual cap, US metropolitan areas could have created as many as 231,224 additional jobs for US-born technology workers. Many of these jobs could have gone to workers without college degrees.Based on H-1B petitions in computer-related occupations rejected by US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) in FY24 and FY25 because of the annual cap, NFAP estimated that a substantially higher annual limit could have supported the creation of up to 615,000 additional jobs for US-born technology workers.Immigration could also have fiscal benefits. Research by former Congressional Budget Office director Douglas Elmendorf and Dartmouth economics professor Heidi Williams found that exempting STEM master’s and PhD holders from employment-based green card limits could reduce the US federal budget deficit by $634 billion over 20 years.
Article Summary: A Democratic majority in Congress may shift the tone of the US immigration debate. But it is unlikely to bring immediate policy relief for Indian technology professionals or employers. Experts believe a Democratic victory could help temper anti-immigrant sentiment and the political rhetoric targeting Indian tech professionals.

Article Title: Ficci seeks exemption from LTCG for listed shares
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Industry body Ficci has sought restoration of long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) exemption on listed securities, while "appropriately" raising the securities transaction tax (STT) on delivery-based transactions to protect govt revenue.During a pre-budget meeting with revenue secretary Arvind Shrivastava on Wednesday, the industry lobby group also suggested that the regime should be maintained for a long period -- possibly 10 years -- to provide stability and certainty to investors.Citing withdrawals of over Rs 3 lakh crore by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) during the year, Ficci said there was a need to review capital gains taxation to improve investment attractiveness. It said the reintroduction of LTCG tax in 2018, without withdrawal of STT, resulted in a dual levy. Since July, govt has increased short-term capital gains tax to 20%, with LTCG beyond the Rs 1.25 lakh exemption threshold pegged at 12.5%."Higher capital gains tax, continued STT and no forex adjustment erode post-tax equity returns," Ficci said, while seeking simplicity, fairness and stability in capital gains taxation. In recent weeks, amid demands for a review of the tax regime, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that govt will watch the debate before taking a call in the budget.Ficci called for exempting B2B payments liable to GST and made to GST-registered suppliers from 0.1% TDS on purchase of goods and e-commerce transactions. TDS for payments to non-GST-registered suppliers may be continued, it said.
Article Summary: Ficci has sought restoration of long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) exemption on listed securities. The industry lobby group also suggested that the regime should be maintained for a long period -- possibly 10 years. Ficci called for exempting B2B payments liable to GST and made to GST-registered suppliers.

Article Title: Oil's slide lifts rupee, gold up 3%
Article Text: MUMBAI: With chances of a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict rising after the Democratic sweep of the mid-term elections, oil prices dipped on Wednesday. In evening trades, Brent crude was down 2.8% at just above the psychologically important $100 level, down from $117 level last week. Falling crude prices also had a positive impact on the rupee that strengthened 10 paise to close at 94.65 to the dollar, a two-week closing high. Gold , meanwhile, surged about 3%, on track for its biggest daily gain since mid-Aug. Spot gold was up 2.9% to $4,040 per ounce.
Article Summary: Brent crude was down 2.8% at just above the psychologically important $100 level, down from $117 level last week. Falling crude prices also had a positive impact on the rupee that strengthened 10 paise to close at 94.65 to the dollar. Gold, meanwhile, surged about 3%, on track for its biggest daily gain since mid- Aug.

Article Title: Cabinet nod for Rs 2,814 cr plan to support critical mineral processing
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Stepping up efforts to reduce dependence on imports of critical minerals, cabinet Wednesday approved a Rs 2,814 crore scheme to boost domestic processing of lithium and nickel.PM Narendra Modi said India cannot afford to depend on other countries for processing such materials and the scheme had been approved to encourage domestic investment and secure future supplies. “Do you feel India should depend on other countries for processing the critical minerals that power our future? I certainly don’t! Lithium, nickel, cobalt…these are essential for EVs, batteries, electronics and defence. Yet, we remain heavily dependent on imports of refined materials,” PM said on X.“To address this, the Cabinet has approved a scheme to change this. Key highlights: New critical mineral processing plants. Capital subsidy to boost investment. Greater domestic value addition. Stronger supply chains. The principle is clear...India must have capabilities to build technologies of the future,” he added.Ministry of mines said processing of critical minerals was geographically concentrated in a few global locations.The scheme aims at developing domestic processing capabilities, promote value addition within the country and reduce import dependence by providing targeted capital expenditure support for setting up and operationalising processing facilities. Commercial-scale projects face challenges such as high capital requirements, limited availability of suitable technologies and constrained access to raw materials.“The scheme targets processing of lithium and nickel ores/intermediary products into high purity compounds. Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production. This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, battery energy storage system, electronics, defence, speciality steel etc,” the ministry said in a statement.India is substantially dependent on imports of refined intermediates and high-purity materials, exposing its supply chains to geopolitical disruptions and price volatility and posing a serious threat to economic security. “This has implications for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely achievement of decarbonisation targets,” it said.Under the scheme, which will be implemented until FY31, capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four critical mineral processing plants - two lithium processing plants with a minimum capacity of 30,000 tonnes each and two nickel processing plants with a minimum capacity of 50,000 tonnes each. The maximum capital support will be capped at Rs 500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs 900 crore per nickel beneficiary.Two beneficiaries for each mineral will be selected through technical and financial bidding, based on the lowest capital support sought.India is substantially dependent on imports of refined intermediates and high-purity materials, exposing its supply chains to geopolitical disruptions and price volatility and posing a serious threat to economic security. “This has implications for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely achievement of decarbonisation targets,” the ministry said.Industry players have termed the scheme an important intervention to address one of the biggest gaps in India’s critical mineral value chain - domestic processing capacity.“While India is taking steps to secure access to critical mineral resources, building the ability to process them into high-purity materials is equally important to reducing import dependence and strengthening supply chain security. The scheme’s focus on lithium and nickel processing can encourage private investment, support technology development and lay the foundation for domestic value addition,” said Nitin Gupta, co-founder and CEO of Attero, a critical minerals technology company that has developed recycling technologies and processing capabilities.“Our experience demonstrates the potential of technology-led processing to strengthen domestic resource security. Together with the recycling incentive scheme, this initiative can help build a genuinely circular and self-reliant supply chain for India’s batteries, electric mobility, energy storage and other strategic sectors,” Gupta added.Prassann Daphal, CEO of Evergreen Recyclekaro India, said critical mineral processing is capital-intensive and involves long gestation periods, which have deterred several Indian companies from entering the space. “The scheme can help bridge this gap and encourage investments, technology partnerships and collaborative ventures,” Daphal said.
Article Summary: Cabinet approves Rs 2,814 crore scheme to boost domestic processing of lithium and nickel. PM Narendra Modi said India cannot afford to depend on other countries for processing such materials. Scheme aims at developing domestic processing capabilities, promote value addition within the country and reduce import dependence.
